methodology: The fabrication process involved spin coating different polymers to create bilayer polymer films that could respond to temperature, magnetic field, solvent vapors, and light by bending or twisting. Interlayer adhesion was improved through plasma and ozone oxidation treatments. The characterization of the fabricated films included optical microscopy, atomic force microscopy, UV-vis spectroscopy, FTIR (Fourier Transform Infrared) spectroscopy, and Raman spectroscopy.
research_objective: To develop stimuli-responsive self-folding bilayer polymer films with enhanced interlayer adhesion for various applications such as micromanipulation, lab-on-a-chip devices, artificial muscles, sensors, drug delivery systems, and tissue engineering.

key_findings.finding: Fabrication of stimuli-responsive self-folding bilayer polymer films with improved interlayer adhesion through plasma and ozone oxidation
Development of new concept of stimuli-responsive homopolymer films doped with various species such as metal ions, molecules or nanoparticles for micromanipulation applications
Self-folding of bilayer polymer films (BPF) into three-dimensional helical structures can be achieved through anisotropic surface stress produced in the layers by external stimuli.
The formation of helical structures in single-component polymer films is also possible, driven by elastic modulus and residual strain or surface stress that are anisotropic [10,18].
Fabrication methods to improve adhesion between polymer layers, rendering the films stable against delamination after repeated exposure to stimuli.
